results.content:
## 10 Best Alternatives & Competitors to Cloudflare

### 1. Akamai

Website:Launched: 1998  
Features: CDN, DDoS protection, web application firewall, and edge computing.  
Is it free?: No, pricing is enterprise-focused.

Akamai is a pioneer in CDN services, offering unparalleled global coverage and robust security. It’s tailored for enterprises requiring advanced scalability and features like bot management and video delivery optimization. This Cloudflare alternative stands out for its reliability and breadth of services, making it a top choice for large-scale operations.

### 2. AWS CloudFront

Website:Launched: 2008  
Features: CDN, DDoS protection, edge computing, and seamless AWS integration.  
Is it free?: Free tier available; pay-as-you-go pricing. [...] AWS CloudFront is an excellent option for those already using AWS services. Its deep integration with other AWS tools makes it ideal for developers seeking a scalable and efficient CDN. This Cloudflare competitor service provides advanced security features and global distribution.

### 3. Fastly

Website:Launched: 2011  
Features: Real-time CDN, WAF, and edge computing.  
Is it free?: Free trial available; pay-as-you-go pricing.

Fastly is a developer-centric platform that emphasizes speed and flexibility. It’s well-suited for dynamic content delivery, such as streaming and real-time updates. This Cloudflare replacement option is popular among companies requiring low-latency performance and customizable configurations.

### 4. Bunny.net [...] ### 4. Bunny.net

Website:Launched: 2014  
Features: CDN, storage, and image optimization.  
Is it free?: No, but it offers affordable pricing plans starting at $1/month.

Bunny.net is a budget-friendly CDN known for its ease of use and effective performance. It caters to small to medium-sized businesses, offering features like bandwidth optimization and caching. This alternatives to Cloudflare is ideal for those seeking simplicity without sacrificing functionality.

### 5. KeyCDN

Website:Launched: 2012  
Features: CDN, origin shield, and real-time analytics.  
Is it free?: No, pay-as-you-go pricing model.

results.title: Cloudflare Alternatives: Which One Is Right for You?
results.content:
### Developer control and edge functionality

If your team thrives on Cloudflare Workers or edge compute tools, you’ll want an alternative that offers the same flexibility, or better.

Platforms like Fastly’s Compute@Edge and Netlify’s Edge Functions help you fine-tune control over caching, routing, and logic execution.

The ability to purge instantly, customize headers, or execute logic close to users is also a huge advantage for dynamic apps and personalized content delivery.

### Transparent pricing and predictable costs

Cloudflare’s usage-based pricing, along with extras for Argo, Workers, and egress, can lead to unexpected charges. [...] ### 6. GCore

If Cloudflare is overkill for your use case, consider Gcore’s rapidly growing global CDN and edge services. The platform is headquartered in Luxembourg, offers 180+ PoPs across six continents, and delivers fast, secure content with strong regional coverage.

Gcore pros

 Cost-effective and average response times hover around 30 ms, making it competitive with top-tier CDNs.
 Feature-rich edge platform: Includes HTTP/2–3, Anycast routing, image optimization (WebP/AVIF), live streaming, edge rules, origin shielding, and raw logs.
 Protection across L3–L7 (DDoS, basic WAF) and next-gen WAAP tools from StackPath.
 High trust scores, with users noting responsiveness and ease of use.

Gcore limitations [...] KeyCDN pros

 Budget-friendly performance (about $0.04/GB) across North America and Europe, with free shared and custom SSL, making it a cost-effective alternative to Cloudflare for small to mid-sized sites.
 Ease of use: Expect a clean UI, straightforward setup, and a strong knowledge base.
 Decent feature set that supports HTTP/2, origin push/pull, token authentication, geo-blocking, hotlink protection, and video-on-demand zones. That’s comparable to more expensive CDNs.
 Transparent support: Some users report slow response times, but positive support experiences are also common, particularly when issues involve their host.

The best Cloudflare WAF alternatives in 2026 are AppTrana WAAP, Akamai Kona Site Defender, Imperva Cloud WAF, Fastly, and AWS WAF. AppTrana is the closest managed alternative: it includes a 24/7 security team, zero false positive SLA, and DDoS protection bundled in every plan. Akamai is the strongest alternative for edge-scale infrastructure. Imperva suits teams needing hybrid deployment and strong false positive control out of the box. [...] Disclosure and perspective:Our observations in this guide are based on public documentation and anonymized patterns we see during customer migrations away from Cloudflare across plan tiers, including Cloudflare Enterprise. 

If you are reading this guide, the intent is likely not “is Cloudflare good?” The intent is that your requirements changed. The most common trigger we see is that the operational burden and risk tolerance shift as traffic grows, APIs expand, compliance expectations rise, and false positives become more expensive. 

The best Cloudflare WAF alternatives in 2026 are AppTrana WAAP, Akamai, Imperva, Fastly, and AWS WAF, each suited to a different operating model, from fully managed protection to self-managed and cloud-native deployments. Even in the above alternatives, AppTrana and Imperva are cost-effective, especially when you want to protect hundreds of applications.

| Google Cloud CDN | Delivery through Google Cloud load balancing | Backend configuration, cache policy, security enforcement scope | [...] Azion, Fastly, Akamai, Amazon CloudFront, Google Cloud CDN, and Vercel offer options for different parts of this decision. Compare them against the requests your team needs to deliver and protect.

## Understanding your Cloudflare replacement scope

A Cloudflare alternative replaces the capabilities you use in a particular workload. Define that workload before comparing vendors: a public website, a storefront, or an API may require different combinations of delivery, execution, and protection.

Start with an inventory. Record your domains, caching rules, redirects, and certificates. List request-processing code and its dependencies, including storage bindings and external services. Ask your security team to document policy exceptions and the incident procedures it needs to preserve.
